basic_information.name: Cohere Embed v3 / v4 (embed-english-v3.0, embed-multilingual-v3.0, embed-v4.0)
basic_information.creator: Cohere (Toronto, Canada)
basic_information.description: Cohere's enterprise-focused embedding model family, spanning text-only v3 (November 2023) and multimodal v4 (April 2025). Embed v3 introduced native int8 and binary quantization with 1024-dimensional embeddings across 100+ languages, achieving state-of-the-art MTEB and BEIR scores at launch. Embed v4 (also called Embed 4) is a major upgrade: multimodal (text + images + interleaved documents), 128K token context window, Matryoshka embeddings (256/512/1024/1536 dimensions), and support for float/int8/uint8/binary/ubinary output formats. Embed v4 scores 65.2% on MTEB, leading proprietary models, and powers Cohere's Compass enterprise search platform and the North agentic AI platform. A key differentiator is Cohere's focus on enterprise deployment flexibility — models can run on Cohere's cloud, AWS (Bedrock, SageMaker), Azure, Oracle Cloud, or on-premise VPC — combined with a strong reranking model (Rerank 3.5/4) that forms a complete retrieval stack. Pricing is competitive at $0.10/1M tokens (v3) and $0.12/1M tokens (v4 text), with $0.47/1M image tokens for v4.
basic_information.release_date: Embed v3: November 2, 2023. Embed v4 (embed-v4.0 / Embed 4): April 15, 2025.
basic_information.license: Proprietary (API-only access for cloud deployments; private/VPC deployment available for enterprise customers; no open model weights). Embed v3 model card is published on Hugging Face for documentation purposes but weights are gated.
basic_information.github_stars: N/A — proprietary API model. Cohere's cohere-python SDK has ~1,000+ GitHub stars. cohere-aws repository has examples. No standalone open-source repository for the embedding models.

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Cloud API (serverless) with enterprise deployment options. Models are hosted on Cohere's infrastructure and accessed via REST API. Also available as managed deployments on AWS Bedrock, AWS SageMaker JumpStart, Azure AI Foundry, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Generative AI Service. Enterprise customers can deploy in Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) or on-premise for data sovereignty requirements. Compass platform provides a managed search index layer on top of Embed.
technical_architecture.language: Model implementation undisclosed. Client SDKs available in Python (cohere), TypeScript/JavaScript (cohere-js), Go, Java, and Ruby. Cohere API v2 is the latest interface version. Also accessible via AWS SDK (Bedrock), Azure SDK, and OCI SDK on respective cloud platforms.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Embed v3 (standard): 1024 dimensions (fixed). Embed v3 (light): 384 dimensions (fixed, English-only). Embed v4: default 1536 dimensions with Matryoshka Representation Learning — supports 256, 512, 1024, and 1536 dimension outputs configurable via the 'output_dimensions' API parameter. Lower dimensions retain strong performance due to Matryoshka training.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: N/A — Cohere Embed is an embedding generation model, not a vector database. It produces dense vector embeddings compatible with any indexing algorithm (HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, flat, product quantization, etc.) in any vector store. Native support for int8 and binary quantization reduces storage requirements: binary quantization compresses vectors by 32x (1024-dim float32 -> 1024-bit binary), int8 by 4x. Embed v4 adds uint8 and ubinary output formats. The Compass platform internally manages its own vector index.
technical_architecture.scalability: Serverless API with automatic scaling. Rate limits on Trial key: 5 calls/minute for Embed endpoint, 1,000 total API calls/month. Production keys have higher limits (contact Cohere for enterprise tiers). Per-request batch limit: up to 96 texts per API call. Embed v4 supports up to 128K tokens per individual text input. Embed v3 recommended input: up to 512 tokens per text (hard limit higher). Embed Jobs API available for asynchronous batch processing of large datasets stored on Cohere's platform.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Cohere Platform (cloud API), AWS Bedrock (fully managed), AWS SageMaker JumpStart (managed hosting), Azure AI Foundry (managed), Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Generative AI Service, Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) deployment for enterprise customers, on-premise deployment for sovereign AI requirements. This multi-cloud and private deployment flexibility is a key enterprise differentiator vs. OpenAI (cloud-only) and Voyage AI.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Dense vector retrieval. Embed models produce dense embeddings optimized for cosine similarity, dot product, and Euclidean distance. The required 'input_type' parameter (search_document, search_query, classification, clustering, image) creates query-document asymmetric embeddings that improve retrieval quality — queries and documents are encoded differently. No native sparse vector (BM25/SPLADE) generation, but Cohere provides guidance for hybrid search combining Embed with BM25 via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF). Embed v4 enables multimodal retrieval: text-to-text, text-to-image, and text-to-mixed-modality (interleaved text+image documents).
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: N/A — embedding model is agnostic to chunking strategy. Works with any chunking approach. The Compass platform handles document parsing and chunking automatically for PDF, PPTX, DOCX, and XLSX files. Embed v4's 128K token context window enables embedding entire documents (up to ~200 pages) without chunking, which is useful for dense legal, financial, and technical documents. Embed v3's 512-token recommended input size requires traditional chunking strategies. Compatible with all chunking frameworks (LangChain splitters, LlamaIndex nodes, Unstructured, etc.).
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Strong built-in reranking ecosystem via companion Cohere Rerank models (Rerank 3.5, Rerank 4). Rerank acts as a cross-encoder second stage in the retrieval pipeline: initial candidates retrieved by Embed are re-scored for relevance by Rerank. This two-stage (Embed + Rerank) pipeline is a core Cohere value proposition. Rerank supports 100+ languages, processes pairs of query+document for relevancy scoring, and can be added to any existing retrieval flow. Rerank is priced separately ($2/1K searches for Rerank 3.5).
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Embed v3: Text-only (no image, audio, or video support). Embed v4: Full multimodal support for text and images. Embed v4 can process interleaved text and image content natively, enabling embedding of complex business documents containing tables, charts, diagrams, code snippets, and handwritten notes without requiring separate OCR preprocessing. Text-to-image search and image-to-text search are both supported. No audio or video embedding.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No native graph capabilities. Cohere Embed produces embeddings only. Knowledge graph construction, entity extraction, and graph-enhanced retrieval must be implemented externally using tools like LlamaIndex's KnowledgeGraphIndex, Microsoft's GraphRAG, or LangChain's graph integrations. The North platform focuses on agentic search rather than graph-based retrieval.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Cohere's Command R/R+ models include built-in grounded generation with inline citations when used in RAG mode. When Embed is used for retrieval and Command R+ for generation, the system can produce responses with source citations pointing back to the retrieved documents. The Compass platform integrates this end-to-end. This is a differentiator vs. OpenAI embeddings, where citation/grounding must be handled at the application layer.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Embed v3: Recommended input up to 512 tokens per text. Documents exceeding this should be chunked externally. Embed v4: 128K token context window — supports embedding extremely long documents (up to ~200 pages) in a single embedding, eliminating the need for chunking in many use cases. This is the largest context window among proprietary embedding models as of early 2026. Matryoshka dimension reduction (e.g., 1536 -> 512 or 256) enables storage and retrieval speed optimization without re-embedding. Binary and int8 quantization further reduce memory footprint by 4-32x.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Embed v3: Query encoding latencies as low as ~5ms reported on optimized deployments. API latency depends on deployment platform, input length, and batch size. Embed v4: Higher latency for long-context inputs (128K tokens) compared to short inputs. Specific p50/p99 numbers vary by deployment (Cohere API vs. Bedrock vs. SageMaker). Oracle Cloud benchmarks provide detailed latency tables across token lengths (64, 128, 256, 512, 1024, 2048, 8096, 32000, 128000 tokens). [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Per-request batch limit of 96 texts. Rate limits depend on plan tier (Trial: 5 calls/minute for Embed). Embed Jobs API enables bulk batch processing for large corpus embedding. Throughput varies significantly across deployment options (Cohere Platform vs. Bedrock vs. SageMaker dedicated endpoints). [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: Embed v3 (embed-english-v3.0): MTEB average score 64.5%, BEIR score 55.9%. Embed v3 (embed-multilingual-v3.0): Strong multilingual retrieval across 100+ languages. Embed v4 (embed-v4.0): MTEB average score 65.2% — highest among proprietary embedding models as of early 2025, ahead of OpenAI text-embedding-3-large (64.6%). Embed v4 also achieves state-of-the-art on text-to-image retrieval and text-to-mixed-modality retrieval benchmarks.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark): Embed v4 scores 65.2%, Embed v3 English scores 64.5%. BEIR (retrieval benchmark): Embed v3 English scores 55.9%. Embed v4 achieves state-of-the-art across text-to-text, text-to-image, and text-to-mixed modality retrieval tasks. For comparison: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large scores 64.6% MTEB, while Voyage-4-large (2026) surpasses Embed v4 by an average of 8.2% across benchmarks. Embed v4 with reduced 512 dimensions (from 1536) shows almost no retrieval quality loss, demonstrating effective Matryoshka training. Binary quantization of Embed v3 retains ~90% of float performance while reducing storage by 32x.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Strong framework integration: LangChain (CohereEmbeddings class in langchain-cohere package), LlamaIndex (CohereEmbedding in llama-index-embeddings-cohere, with automatic v3/v4 format detection), Haystack (CohereTextEmbedder, CohereDocumentEmbedder, CohereDocumentImageEmbedder components), DSPy (Cohere integration available), Semantic Kernel (Cohere connector). Also directly integrated with vector databases: Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, Chroma, Elasticsearch, and pgvector all have Cohere embedding examples or built-in connectors. LlamaIndex recently fixed BedrockEmbedding to support v4's new response format (PR #20094).
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Embed models produce standard dense vectors usable with any LLM for RAG generation. Most commonly paired with Cohere's own Command R+ and Command A models (which include built-in grounded generation with citations), but equally compatible with OpenAI GPT-4o, Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, Meta Llama, and any other LLM. Works with any vector database. The Embed + Rerank + Command R+ combination is Cohere's recommended full-stack RAG pipeline.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Cohere offers MCP server integration. Third-party MCP servers for Cohere AI exist (viasocket.com/mcp/cohere-ai, Zapier MCP for Cohere). Cohere's Command models support dynamic MCP tool calling for agentic workflows. The integration is actively evolving as part of the broader MCP ecosystem adoption in 2025-2026.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Embed API is a pure embedding generation API — data source connectivity is handled by orchestration frameworks. The Compass platform provides built-in document parsing for PDF, PPTX, DOCX, and XLSX files with managed indexing. Through LangChain/LlamaIndex integrations, Cohere Embed works with all standard data source loaders: S3, GCS, Confluence, Notion, Slack, databases, web crawl, etc. Cohere also provides Embed Jobs API for bulk processing datasets stored on their platform.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Cohere provides a dashboard for API usage monitoring. Compatible with third-party observability platforms through LangChain/LlamaIndex instrumentation: LangSmith, Langfuse, Arize Phoenix all support Cohere embedding call tracing. OpenTelemetry instrumentation available through integration packages. Cohere's enterprise platform includes audit logging and usage analytics.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Pay-per-token for API usage. Embed v3: $0.10 per million tokens. Embed v4: $0.12 per million tokens (text), $0.47 per million tokens (images). No subscription or per-seat fees for API access. Enterprise pricing for VPC/on-premise deployments is custom (contact Cohere). Compass platform pricing is separate. Embed Jobs API for batch processing may have different pricing.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Trial API key: 1,000 free API calls per month across all endpoints (including Embed), with access to all models including Embed 4, Command R+, and Rerank 3.5. Rate limits on Trial: 5 calls/minute for Embed, 20 calls/minute for Chat. Free tier is for testing and development only, not production use.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Embed v3 at $0.10/1M tokens: 1M documents (~500 tokens each = 500M tokens) costs $50. 10M documents: $500. Embed v4 text at $0.12/1M tokens: 1M documents costs $60, 10M documents costs $600. Embed v4 images at $0.47/1M tokens: significantly higher for image-heavy workloads. Cost comparison with OpenAI: Embed v3 is 5x more expensive than text-embedding-3-small ($0.02/1M) but cheaper than text-embedding-3-large ($0.13/1M). Embed v4 is slightly cheaper than text-embedding-3-large. Binary/int8 quantization reduces downstream vector storage costs by 4-32x.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Full RAG pipeline TCO with Cohere stack: Embed ($0.10-0.12/1M tokens for embedding) + Rerank ($2/1K searches for second-stage reranking) + Command R+ ($2.50/$10 per 1M input/output tokens for generation). The reranking cost is often the most significant per-query component. Vector database hosting adds $20-500+/month depending on scale. Enterprise VPC/on-premise deployment pricing is custom but typically involves significant upfront licensing. Using Matryoshka dimension reduction (e.g., 512 instead of 1536) and binary quantization can cut vector storage costs by 10-30x. Compass managed platform bundles embedding, indexing, and search into a single price point.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Strong challenger to OpenAI in the enterprise embedding market, with growing adoption particularly among enterprises requiring data sovereignty, multi-cloud deployment, or on-premise options. Cohere positions itself as the enterprise-first AI company, with Embed being a core component of its Compass search platform and North agentic AI suite. Embed v4's multimodal capabilities and 128K context window represent technical leadership among proprietary embedding models. Market share is smaller than OpenAI's embedding API but growing rapidly, especially in regulated industries (finance, healthcare, government) where Cohere's deployment flexibility is a significant advantage.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Enterprise customers using Cohere's platform (which includes Embed): Oracle, Dell, RBC (Royal Bank of Canada), Bell Canada, Fujitsu, LG CNS, SAP, Notion, and Ensemble Health Partners. Cohere reports that approximately 85% of revenue comes from private deployments, indicating strong enterprise adoption. The company has multi-year contracts with large enterprises across finance, healthcare, telecommunications, manufacturing, energy, and public sector verticals.
adoption_and_market.community_size: Cohere's developer community is smaller than OpenAI's but highly enterprise-focused. cohere-python SDK: ~1,000+ GitHub stars. Active Discord community. Developer documentation is comprehensive with extensive tutorials and cookbooks. Community engagement is growing through partnerships with AWS, Azure, and Oracle. Monthly API users and exact community numbers not publicly disclosed.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Cohere raised $500 million in Series D (August 2025) at a $6.8 billion valuation, led by Radical Ventures and Inovia Capital with participation from AMD Ventures, NVIDIA, PSP Investments, and Salesforce Ventures. Extended the round by $100 million in September 2025, reaching a $7 billion valuation with AMD partnership. The company crossed $100 million in annual recurring revenue (ARR) in May 2025 and expects to exceed $200 million ARR by end of 2025. Total funding: well over $1 billion across all rounds.
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: OpenAI text-embedding-3 (market leader by adoption, 64.6% MTEB, text-only, cloud-only), Voyage AI (now part of Google/Alphabet; Voyage-4 at ~68.6% MTEB, strong domain-specific models for code/legal/finance), Google Gemini Embedding (Vertex AI ecosystem, competitive multilingual), Amazon Titan Embeddings (AWS ecosystem), Jina Embeddings (open-source + API). Open-source alternatives: BGE (BAAI), E5 (Microsoft), GTE (Alibaba), Nomic Embed — several match or exceed Cohere on MTEB at zero API cost. Cohere differentiates via: enterprise deployment flexibility (VPC/on-premise), complete retrieval stack (Embed + Rerank + Command), multimodal document understanding in v4, 128K context window, Compass managed search platform, and strong multilingual support.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Best for: startups building enterprise-grade RAG applications where data sovereignty, multi-cloud deployment, or on-premise requirements exist (regulated industries like fintech, healthtech, legaltech). Also ideal for multilingual products targeting 100+ languages. The Embed + Rerank + Command R+ stack provides a single-vendor RAG solution with built-in grounded generation and citations. Team size: works for teams of any size, but the enterprise deployment options are most valuable for teams of 10+ with compliance requirements. Budget: moderate entry cost ($0.10-0.12/1M tokens), higher than OpenAI small but competitive with OpenAI large. The free trial (1,000 calls/month) is sufficient for initial prototyping but limited for serious development. Consider OpenAI for lower-cost prototyping, or open-source models for zero-cost alternatives.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Cohere Embed API (buy) when: enterprise data sovereignty or multi-cloud deployment is required, you need multimodal document search (v4), the complete Embed+Rerank+Command stack reduces integration complexity, or multilingual support across 100+ languages is needed. Use Compass (managed buy) when: you want a fully managed search platform without managing vector databases or retrieval pipelines. Consider self-hosted open-source models when: API costs are prohibitive at scale, you need fine-tuning for a specific domain, or you want to eliminate vendor dependency entirely. Cohere's VPC deployment is a middle ground between pure API and fully self-hosted. Migration note: switching from Cohere to another embedding model requires re-embedding your entire corpus, as embeddings from different models are not interchangeable.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 30-60 minutes (pip install cohere + simple API call with input_type parameter). MVP with full RAG pipeline using LangChain/LlamaIndex: 2-5 days. Production deployment on Cohere Platform: 2-4 weeks including error handling, rate limit management, and monitoring. Enterprise VPC/on-premise deployment: 4-12 weeks depending on infrastructure requirements and compliance review. Compass managed platform can accelerate time-to-production by handling document parsing, indexing, and search management.
key_lessons: 1. Leverage the input_type parameter correctly — it is required for v3+ and significantly impacts retrieval quality. Always use 'search_document' for indexing and 'search_query' for queries. Using the wrong type (or the same type for both) degrades retrieval performance noticeably.

2. Start with Embed v4 at 512 dimensions instead of 1536 — Cohere's Matryoshka training means 512-dim vectors achieve nearly identical retrieval quality to 1536-dim but use 3x less storage. This is a 3x reduction in vector database costs with minimal quality impact. Only increase dimensions if measured retrieval quality demands it.

3. Use the Embed + Rerank two-stage pipeline — Cohere's Rerank model (3.5 or 4) adds a cross-encoder re-scoring step that dramatically improves precision. The combination outperforms either model alone. Budget for reranking cost ($2/1K searches) as it is often the largest per-query expense.

4. Binary quantization is production-ready for large-scale deployments — Embed v3/v4's native binary output retains ~90% of float retrieval quality while reducing storage by 32x. For 10M+ document collections, this can cut vector database costs from hundreds to tens of dollars per month.

5. Cohere's enterprise deployment flexibility is a strategic advantage for regulated industries — if your startup targets finance, healthcare, or government, the ability to deploy Embed in a VPC or on-premise (without data leaving customer infrastructure) can be the difference between closing and losing enterprise deals. Plan deployment architecture early.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: The Compass platform provides a managed search service that abstracts away embedding, indexing, and retrieval complexity — approaching no-code for search use cases with built-in document parsing (PDF, PPTX, DOCX, XLSX). The Cohere Playground offers a web-based interface for testing embeddings. The North platform provides a higher-level workspace for building AI applications. Third-party no-code platforms (Flowise, Dify, AnythingLLM, Relevance AI) also integrate with Cohere's embedding API.

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from Cohere's official documentation (docs.cohere.com), Cohere's blog announcements, AWS documentation (Bedrock and SageMaker), Oracle Cloud documentation, independent benchmark comparisons (MTEB leaderboard, Pinecone, ZenML, Ailog), pricing pages, and enterprise press coverage (TechCrunch, BetaKit, SiliconANGLE, VentureBeat).
confidence.cross_reference: MTEB scores confirmed across multiple sources: Embed v3 English at 64.5% (Cohere blog, MarkTechPost, Zilliz), Embed v4 at 65.2% (Ailog, AiMultiple, beyond-bot.ai). Pricing confirmed: $0.10/1M tokens (v3), $0.12/1M tokens (v4 text), $0.47/1M image tokens (MetaCTO, Holori calculator). Funding/valuation confirmed across Cohere blog, TechCrunch, BetaKit, Crunchbase ($500M at $6.8B, then $7B). 128K context window for v4 and Matryoshka dimensions confirmed across Cohere docs, AWS docs, and multiple blog posts. Enterprise customer list confirmed from Cohere website, investor announcements.
confidence.caveats: MTEB scores may differ between MTEB v1 and v2 leaderboard methodologies — the 65.2% for Embed v4 is from MTEB v1. Voyage-4 (January 2026) surpasses Embed v4 by a significant margin on many benchmarks. The 137-language claim from the research notes was not confirmed — official documentation states '100+ languages' for both v3 and v4. Specific latency and throughput numbers are deployment-dependent and not consistently published by Cohere. Enterprise VPC/on-premise pricing is not publicly disclosed. The Compass platform is evolving rapidly and features may change. Cohere's $200M ARR target for end of 2025 may not have been publicly confirmed as achieved.
confidence.security_posture: Cohere's infrastructure is SOC 2 Type II certified (annual audit), ISO 27001 compliant, and HITRUST compliant. Data encrypted at rest (AES-256) and in transit (TLS). GDPR compliant with Data Processing Addendum (DPA) available. Privacy-by-Design approach with customer data never used for model training. Enterprise deployments can be fully isolated in VPC or on-premise to ensure data never leaves customer infrastructure. This is a significant security advantage over cloud-only embedding APIs. Known general embedding risks: embedding vectors can theoretically be inverted to approximate original text (embedding inversion attacks), which is a general risk across all embedding models, not specific to Cohere.
